correctness.rationale: The finite Boolean-filter representation decomposes every finite ADA into two- and three-element coordinates. Explicit crisp tests construct selectors for pairwise distinct generator words, with undefined values obtained only where present. Independent falling-factorial assignment counts follow. Collision factorial moments give Poisson(a²/2), missing-U words give Poisson(b), and ternary collisions vanish as O((3/4)^k). The standalone exhaustive checker reproduces twelve finite counts. Full generality follows from the written proof, not finite testing.

value.rationale: The result answers a natural average-case generation question for recently unified three-valued algebraic semantics. It distinguishes the Boolean birthday obstruction from a qualitatively different ternary missing-undefined obstruction, identifies two competing exponential coordinate scales and the full nondegenerate limiting law. These features are useful in random generation, finite-model sampling and benchmark design beyond deterministic generator rank.
